_comment: Facts about this adapter that its probe response cannot carry: display names, maturity, and the engine versions CI actually restores from. Everything the probe declares (adapter version, engine id, source kinds, pitr) is read from testdata/probe_response.golden instead — never duplicated here. The capabilities generator fails if the source names below do not match the probe exactly, and the integration suite restores from the images listed under verified — the baseline on every run — so neither can drift. Unlike the Cassandra image, this one does not idle under `command: sleep infinity`: its entrypoint appends the container command to the server's own argv, so that command makes the server exit with 'too many positional options' before it serves anything (measured 2026-09-20). The sandbox therefore runs the engine and the drill config passes the engine's own flags as the command — `--smp 1` is what makes a small sandbox viable, and below about 2 GiB the server aborts on startup. The vendor's support policy is relative (the two latest versions under active maintenance) rather than a published forward date, so supported_until is null and versions_checked records the reading (docs/engine-versions.md §1). Licence position: docs/engine-licensing.md and the adapter README. See docs/capabilities.md.
name: ScyllaDB

sources.scylladb_snapshot_tar: One tar archive (plain or gzip) of a collected snapshot, keyspaces at the root or under one wrapping directory
sources.scylladb_snapshot: One collected snapshot tree: `<keyspace>/<table>/` holding each table's `snapshots/<tag>/` contents
sources.scylladb_snapshot_dir: A directory of collected snapshot trees; the one whose own manifests claim the newest instant is restored
